correctness.rationale: For each arm i, the number t_i of terminals matched on that arm obeys t_i congruent ell_i-1 modulo 2 and sum_i t_i=2. This proves nonexistence unless the even-arm count is zero or two and forces exactly r, respectively two, perfect matchings. In the all-odd case, the intersection of any proper nonempty selection of matching facets contains an edge on an unselected arm, while the complete intersection has no edge: the nerve is the boundary of an (r-1)-simplex and the nerve theorem yields S^(r-2), with integral homology. In the exactly-two-even case, the remaining odd arms supply a shared edge to the two facets, whose union is contractible. Natural Cech homology of facet intersections yields the sign action of equal-length arm permutations, and terminal reversal fixes facet labels and acts trivially. The companion independent enumerator tested 1424 parameter instances, 182 exact mod-two homology calculations, and 15 signed Lefschetz character comparisons.

originality.rationale: The closest physically inspected primary work [Bayer et al. 2023] uses a nerve cover for hexagonal line tilings and discrete Morse theory for honeycombs, not arbitrarily many disjoint paths between two terminals; the new parity phase diagram and action on integral top homology do not follow. Chandrakar–Singh 2025 concerns polygonal line tilings and ladders, whereas these multi-theta graphs have r>=4 mutually shared two-terminal paths. Agarwal–Basak 2026 concerns cubic Möbius and circular ladders, whereas the current graphs have degree r>=4 at two terminals and degree two elsewhere. Targeted searches in public research records did not identify an exact multi-theta perfect-matching-complex classification, but this is not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Accessible full text of the 2026 Möbius/circular ladder manuscript and the 2025 polygonal-line article was unavailable; no whole-document exclusion claim is made for those works.
Indexed and semantic search retrieval cannot establish global uniqueness: equivalent results may use the terms subdivided dipoles, multi-theta or generalized banana graphs.

The homotopy proof uses the classical nerve theorem; originality attaches to the new forced matching classification, its parity completeness and its integral symmetry action, not to the topological tool.

value.rationale: The natural class of subdivided r-edge dipoles is planar and series-parallel; the even-arm count is an intrinsic structural parameter. The result classifies all perfect-matching complexes in the r>=4 class including existence, contractibility and arbitrarily high-dimensional sphere cases, rather than cherry-picking small boards or postulating a generic wedge. It relates the unique nonzero homological dimension to the cyclomatic number minus one and determines a full integral arm-permutation orientation character. The result remains meaningful as a self-contained topological benchmark for matching-complex methods even without a downstream general theorem.
